subject: rabbit
readings: head at +x: nose tip ~(19,8), ear tip ~(14,0) in XY panel -> XY panel is the PROFILE (nose-to-tail runs along x, height along y); ZY panel is the FRONT view (z is the animal's left-right width, matches the ~17-unit width seen in the XZ top view); XZ panel is the TOP view (x nose-tail, z left-right)
spine readings (XY panel): pelvis/root ~(6,11), spine_mid ~(10,9), withers ~(13,8) - back rises gently from rump to shoulders
neck/head: withers (13,8) to neck (13,8)->nose tip (19,8); ear tip (14,0) confirms head sits atop a short neck
front leg (XY panel): shoulder ~(13,9), knee/elbow ~(15,15), paw ~(16,21); ground line ~y=21-22
hind leg (XY panel): hip ~(5,10), hock ~(8,16), paw ~(10,21); hind leg tucked under body typical of sitting rabbit
tail (XY panel): base ~(2,11) at rear of rump, tip ~(0,14) - small downward tail bump
left/right offset taken from XZ top view: body center z~8.5, width 0-17, so left/right limbs offset by +/-3 in z from the spine
notes: Sitting rabbit. XY panel is the profile (head at +x, ears/snout on the right); the ZY panel, despite showing a similarly tall silhouette, is actually the front view because the animal's ears and splayed front paws give it comparable left-right (z) spread; the XZ panel is the top-down view and confirms x is the long nose-tail axis (spanning ~21 units) while z is the narrower left-right width (~17 units). Front and hind legs are each split into two segments (shoulder->knee->paw, hip->hock->paw) since the exact knee/hock bend isn't a sharply marked landmark but is anatomically required for a rabbit's crouched stance - this split is inferred, not directly measured. The small tail bump at the rear (x~0-2) was split into base/tip for a minimal one-segment flap. Left/right limb pairs are each given independent chains back to the spine (withers for forelegs, pelvis for hind legs) per the two-frame instructions, offset in z using the top-view body width as a proxy for left/right placement. Ears, eyes and other head detail were not counted as separate leaves per the sub-flap rule.
